title: L4 moves connections fast; L7 reads the request and routes it
caption: A common stack: a network (L4) LB in front of a fleet of L7 proxies that terminate TLS and route by path.

steps.text: The L4 LB sees only IPs and ports. It picks a proxy per connection and forwards packets without reading them: millions of connections, little CPU.
The L7 proxy terminates TLS and reads the HTTP request: method, path, headers, cookies.
Now it can route by content (/api to one service, /img to another), retry a failed backend, and add auth or headers.
